metrics.name: fragment_vs_word_onset_similarity
metrics.threshold: MFCC cosine > 0.80 = the same onset repeated

regions.explanation: At 9.56s, the onset of “but” is repeated 3 time(s) before the word is completed (fragment-to-onset spectral similarity 0.95). Repeated onsets before the word is completed fragment it and interrupt the speech rhythm. Fix: Begin the word once, deliberately; a short breath before it helps.

regions.text: signifying renewal as well as change. For I
regions.explanation: From 17.58s to 22.82s (“signifying renewal as well as change. For I”), the share of energy above 2 kHz dropped to 0.8% from 2.5% (-68%); that is 2.7× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Energy above 2 kHz carries consonant bursts and fricatives (t, k, s, f); losing it blurs word boundaries and makes the speech sound muffled even at normal volume. Fix: Open the mouth more and finish final consonants crisply.

regions.text: before you and Almighty God the same solemn oath our
regions.explanation: From 23.52s to 27.34s (“before you and Almighty God the same solemn oath our”), articulation rate was 5.53 syll/s against 3.22 syll/s in the reference (+72%); that is 2.3× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Faster articulation compresses the stressed syllables and the micro-pauses listeners use to segment phrases, so key words lose emphasis and comprehension drops. Fix: Slow to the reference pace here and let the pauses between clauses breathe.

regions.text: mortal hands the power to abolish all forms of human poverty and
regions.explanation: From 38.60s to 46.78s (“mortal hands the power to abolish all forms of human …”), pitch range (10th–90th percentile) narrowed to 0.2 st from 5.4 st (-96%); that is 8.2× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Pitch movement is the main cue English listeners use to find the focus word of a phrase; with a flattened contour every word carries equal weight and the line sounds recited. Fix: Lift pitch on the focus word of each clause and let it fall at the end of the thought.

metrics.name: held_steady_voicing
metrics.threshold: steady pitch + unchanging spectrum >= 140 ms longer than reference

regions.explanation: At 48.12s, between “human” and “life.”, a 530 ms held vowel (“uh”/“um”) appears where the reference holds 0 ms, adding 850 ms at this word boundary. A held, unchanging vowel that maps to no word in the transcript is a filled pause; listeners hear it as hesitation, and judges penalise it under fluency. Fix: Replace the filler with silence - a clean pause sounds deliberate.

regions.text: for which our forebears fought are still
regions.explanation: From 55.02s to 58.62s (“for which our forebears fought are still”), loudness relative to the speaker's own level fell 6.9 dB below the reference, bottoming out 11.1 dB down; that is 1.4× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. The loudness falls away across the phrase, so its final words - often the payoff - drop toward the noise floor of the room. Fix: Support the breath through the end of the phrase; the last words need the same energy as the first.
